label: Li Shizhen 時珍
summary: Ming dynasty physician, pharmacologist and naturalist (1518-1593), compiler of the Bencao gangmu.

label: Kou Zongshi 宗奭
summary: Song dynasty pharmacologist (fl. 1110-1119), author of the Bencao yanyi (Dilations on Materia Medica, 1116).

label: Zhang Zhongjing 仲景
summary: Eastern Han physician (c. 150-219), the 'medical sage', author of the Shanghan zabing lun.

label: Bencao gangmu 本草綱目
summary: Running title of the source work itself: Li Shizhen's 52-juan Compendium of Materia Medica (completed 1578, printed 1596).
canonical: Bencao gangmu 本草綱目 (Compendium of Materia Medica), Li Shizhen, 1578/1596

label: huma 胡麻 (sesame)
summary: Sesame; its seed is the smallest unit in the classical pill-size scale.

label: shu 黍 (broomcorn millet)
summary: Broomcorn (proso) millet, one of the two millets named as alternative size-gauges for the smallest pills.

label: su 粟 (foxtail millet)
summary: Foxtail millet, paired with broomcorn millet as a size-gauge for the smallest pills.

label: dama 大麻 (hemp)
summary: Hemp; the hemp seed is the second step of the classical pill-size ladder (one hemp seed = three sesame seeds).

label: hudou 胡荳 / qingbandou 青斑豆
summary: The 'Iranian bean' of the pill-size scale, glossed in the text itself as the contemporary 'green speckled bean'; its botanical identity is disputed.
canonical: uncertain - traditionally identified with Vicia faba L. or Pisum sativum L.

label: chixiaodou 赤小豆 (adzuki / rice bean)
summary: The red small bean (adzuki), equated with the xiaodou gauge (= three hemp seeds).

label: dadou 大豆 (soybean)
summary: The soybean, next step of the pill-size ladder (= two small beans).

label: wuzi 梧子 (wutong seed)
summary: Seed of the wutong (Chinese parasol tree), the commonest pill-size standard in Chinese pharmacy.

label: renshen 人參 (ginseng)
summary: Ginseng root, first ingredient of Zhang Zhongjing's twelve-liang decoction cited as the model of ancient dosage.

label: zhu 朮 (atractylodes)
summary: Atractylodes rhizome, second ingredient of the cited Zhongjing formula; in Han texts the name did not yet distinguish white from cang atractylodes.

label: ganjiang 乾薑 (dried ginger)
summary: Dried ginger rhizome; appears in the cited formula and again in the piece-to-weight rules ('one connected strand = one liang').

label: gancao 甘草 (licorice)
summary: Licorice root, harmoniser of the cited formula; also standardised by length ('one chi = two liang').

label: yangmei 楊梅 (Chinese bayberry)
summary: The Chinese bayberry fruit, invoked as the (too small) pill size used by careless moderns.

label: badou 巴豆 (croton seed)
summary: Croton seed, a drastic purgative: count converted to weight (16 seeds = 1 fen) and pounded to paste among the oily drugs.

label: fuzi 附子 / wutou 烏頭 (aconite)
summary: Aconite: the lateral root (fuzi) and main tuber (wutou) of the same plant, standardised at one piece = half a liang after peeling.

label: zhishi 枳實 (immature bitter orange)
summary: Immature bitter-orange fruit, de-pulped and reckoned at two pieces to the fen.

label: jupi 橘皮 (tangerine peel)
summary: Tangerine peel (chenpi), reckoned at three pieces to the fen.

label: zao 棗 (jujube)
summary: Jujube (Chinese date): three fruits of assorted size are reckoned as one liang.

label: banxia 半夏 (pinellia)
summary: Pinellia tuber: one sheng by volume, after washing, is standardised at five liang.

label: shujiao 蜀椒 (Sichuan pepper)
summary: Sichuan pepper husks: one sheng = three liang.

label: wuzhuyu 吳茱萸 (evodia)
summary: Evodia fruit: one sheng = five liang.

label: tusizi 兎絲子 (dodder seed)
summary: Dodder seed: one sheng = nine liang, the heaviest seed in the table.

label: anluzi 菴蘭子 (keiske wormwood seed)
summary: Seed written 菴蘭子, evidently for anluzi 菴閭子, identified as Artemisia keiskeana: one sheng = four liang.

label: shechuang 蛇床 (cnidium)
summary: Cnidium ('snake's bed') seed: one sheng = three and a half liang; the name runs across the column break.

label: difuzi 地膚子 (kochia seed)
summary: Kochia (broom-plant) seed: one sheng = four liang; seeds that resist weighing are taken by the level sheng.

label: gui 桂 (Chinese cassia)
summary: Cassia bark, standardised by length: one chi, pared of its outer cork, = half a liang.
canonical: Cinnamomum aromaticum Nees (Chinese cassia; C. cassia auct.)

label: tianmendong 天門冬 (asparagus root)
summary: Chinese asparagus tuber, cited as a typical moist drug needing extra weight, separate drying and pounding.

label: dihuang 地黃 (rehmannia)
summary: Rehmannia root, the other named moist drug requiring increased allowance and separate processing.

label: xingren 杏仁 (apricot kernel)
summary: Apricot kernel, listed with croton and sesame among oily drugs to be roasted and pounded to a paste.
